subject: SKU bundling, discount band application & order-form redlines
messages:
From: Sarah Park <sarah@orbitsolutions.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orbitsolutions.com
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification on SKU bundling and pricing exhibit

Hi Marcus / Laura,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement flagged two items in the pricing exhibit/order form that we need clarified before we can sign:

1) SKU bundling: the exhibit references "bundle discounts" but doesn't define whether the discount bands apply per-sku before bundling or to the aggregate bundle. Our billing runs at SKU granularity and we need to know whether your caps/floors and banded discounts will be calculated pre- or post-aggregation.

2) Minimum floor carveout for pilot seats: we requested a temporary carveout for the first quarter's pilot seats (small count, high per-seat rate). The current language appears to treat pilot seats the same as committed seats, which would push us over the initial floor.

Can you point us at the exact clause and suggest wording so legal/procurement can accept?

Also, we'll need any attachments (marked redlines) so our counsel can review.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Park
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Orbit Solutions


From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah@orbitsolutions.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on SKU bundling and pricing exhibit

Hi Sarah — appreciate the fast follow.

Quick answers up front:
- Bundling calculation: Redwood's intent in the exhibit is to apply the discount band to the aggregated bundle (post-aggregation). That yields predictable unit economics and avoids per-sku micro-banding noise.
- Pilot seats: we can accept a 90-day pilot carveout where pilot SKUs are excluded from the annual floor calculation, with a one-time reconciliation at quarter end.

I'm attaching a redline (pricing-exhibit_v3_redline.docx) with two proposed edits:
A) Section 2.1 (Discount bands): add parenthetical language "(for clarity: bundle-level aggregation applies; discounts computed on the consolidated bundle)".
B) Section 3.4 (Commit floors): add a pilot carveout sentence and an annual true-up note.

Attachments: pricing-exhibit_v3_redline.docx (redline doc)

If those are acceptable we'll prepare an updated Order Form (with SKU mapping) and send to your procurement team for signature.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Sales, East
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Sarah Park <sarah@orbitsolutions.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on SKU bundling and pricing exhibit

Thanks Marcus — the proposed edits are on the right track. Two legal notes we'd like to tighten before sending to Orbit legal:

1) Aggregation + rounding: please add explicit rounding rule. Our recommendation: calculate discounts on the aggregated bundle, round per-line to two decimal places using "bankers rounding" and apply invoice-level adjustments only at true-up. This prevents downstream disputes on fractional token/usage billing.

Suggested language (to include in the redline):
"For purposes of the Discount Bands, usage shall be aggregated at the Bundle level. Discount calculations shall be performed on the aggregated quantity and resulting dollar amounts shall be rounded to two decimal places using round-half-to-even (bankers rounding). Any discrepancy arising from rounding shall be reconciled at the next scheduled annual true-up."

2) Pilot carveout: make the carveout conditional on registration of the pilot SKUs within 30 days of start date and cap the carveout to 2% of committed units for the first quarter. This avoids open-ended carveouts.

Also need to confirm treatment of overage caps: are caps measured on billed units or raw usage? Call that out.

I'll fold these into the doc and attach an Order Form skeleton (orderform_SKU-mapping.xlsx) so Orbit procurement can validate the SKU IDs.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Park <sarah@orbitsolutions.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orbitsolutions.com
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on SKU bundling and pricing exhibit

Laura / Marcus — thanks for the quick turn. Procurement reviewed your suggested language and had two follow-ups:

- Rounding: Acceptable. We'll review as long as you include the reconciliation window and an example in the exhibit (small table showing pre/post rounding).
- Pilot carveout: We can agree to registration-within-30-days but cannot accept a hard cap tied to committed units (our internal forecast may shift). Instead we propose: pilot seats are excluded from the floor for the first 90 days and any pilot usage that converts to committed usage within 90 days will be credited toward the annual committed volume at the conversion rate.

Procurement also asked that the Order Form include an explicit "cap measurement" line: either (A) billed units, or (B) raw usage. Their preference is billed units for invoicing clarity. Could you confirm Redwood's measurement?

Lastly, please upload the redlines to the DocuSign envelope or share a Drive folder so our counsel can run a track-change comparison.

Thanks — we'll aim to respond with final procurement comments by EOD Wed.

Best,
Sarah

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah@orbitsolutions.com>, procurement@orbitsolutions.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Final proposed redline + next steps (Orbit Solutions / ORBIT-4532)

Hi Sarah — appreciate the clarity from procurement. Per your feedback we've prepared a consolidated redline and an Order Form skeleton:
- pricing-exhibit_v3_redline.docx: includes the aggregation + bankers rounding clause, pilot carveout language revised to exclude pilot seats for 90 days and to credit conversions toward committed volume if converted within the 90-day window, and a stated measurement definition for caps ("measured on billed units, as invoiced").
- orderform_SKU-mapping.xlsx: SKU ID mapping and example rounding table for the exhibit.
- canary-rollout-ops-note.pdf: operational note describing how bundle aggregation is computed at invoice time (for your billing/ops team).

I've uploaded everything to the Drive link below and added the DocuSign envelope (https://app.docusign.com/envelope/exampledoc123). Please have procurement confirm whether billed-units measurement is acceptable; if yes, we'll circulate the DocuSign-ready Order Form and target signature by next Thursday so we can begin provisioning reserved capacity in July.

Next steps:
1) Orbit procurement confirms billed-units measurement and pilot carveout language by EOD Wed.
2) Redwood will finalize DocuSign envelope and send to signee list.
3) Ops will schedule SKU mapping call if there are mismatches.

Attachments (sent): pricing-exhibit_v3_redline.docx; orderform_SKU-mapping.xlsx; canary-rollout-ops-note.pdf

Thanks and let me know if you want a 20-min call to walk the redline.
